questions.stem: A researcher measures how quickly an oral drug reaches its peak plasma concentration and how long the kidneys take to clear it. Which field is being studied?
questions.explanation: Absorption and excretion are what the body does to the drug: pharmacokinetics (ADME). A: Pharmacodynamics is what the drug does to the body. B: Pharmacogenomics is how genes change response or dose. C: Pharmacoepidemiology is drug behavior across populations. E: Pharmaceutics is drug formulation and delivery.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics relate to each other?

options.A: Pharmacokinetics sets the drug concentration at the site of action; pharmacodynamics translates that concentration into an effect
options.B: Pharmacodynamics sets the drug concentration at the site of action; pharmacokinetics translates it into an effect
options.C: Both describe what the body does to the drug
options.D: Pharmacokinetics describes receptor binding; pharmacodynamics describes drug excretion
options.E: Both describe what the drug does to the body

questions.explanation: PK (body → drug) determines the concentration available at the site of action; PD (drug → body) turns that concentration into effect. B: Reverses the two. C: Only PK is what the body does to the drug; PD is the reverse. D: Receptor binding is PD and excretion is PK. E: Only PD is what the drug does to the body; PK is the reverse.

questions.stem: A patient needs a much lower dose of a drug than most patients because of an inherited variant in the gene for the enzyme that inactivates it. Which discipline best explains this?
questions.explanation: Pharmacogenomics explains why a patient's DNA changes their dose. A: Pharmacoepidemiology looks at drug behavior across whole populations, not one patient's genotype. B: Pharmaceutics is formulation and delivery. C: Toxicology is detecting and treating poisoning. D: Pharmacoeconomics asks whether a drug is worth its cost.

questions.stem: A health ministry compares the price and health outcomes of two antihypertensives to decide which one to reimburse. Which discipline does this analysis belong to?
questions.explanation: Pharmacoeconomics asks whether a drug is worth what it costs. A: Pharmacoepidemiology describes how drugs behave across populations, not cost. B: Pharmacy is preparing, verifying and dispensing drugs. D: Pharmaceutics is formulation and delivery. E: Pharmacodynamics is the drug's effect on the body.

questions.stem: Which historical event most directly led to mandatory teratogenicity testing before drug approval?

options.A: Withering's study of foxglove for dropsy
options.C: The compilation of the Ebers Papyrus
options.D: The isolation of aspirin's active compound from willow bark
options.E: Medicinal cultivation of the opium poppy in Sumer

questions.explanation: Thalidomide, given for morning sickness without fetal testing, caused severe limb malformations; mandatory trial phases, teratogenicity testing and informed consent laws followed. A: Withering established systematic dose testing, not teratogenicity rules. C: The Ebers Papyrus is an ancient list of remedies. D: Willow bark is the origin of aspirin, unrelated to fetal safety rules. E: Opium use in Sumer is ancient history with no regulatory consequence.

questions.stem: William Withering's lasting contribution to pharmacology was best described as:

options.A: The first chemical synthesis of a drug
options.B: Creating the first national drug-approval agency
options.D: Systematic dose testing in patients with recorded outcomes
options.E: Introducing informed consent for clinical trials

questions.explanation: Withering spent nearly a decade testing foxglove doses on patients, recording benefit and harm: observe, dose, record, adjust. A: He identified a plant ingredient; he didn't synthesize a drug. B: Drug agencies came later. C: Receptor theory is unrelated to his work. E: Informed consent laws followed thalidomide in the 1960s.

questions.stem: A newborn has severely shortened limbs with the hands attached close to the shoulders. Early in pregnancy, the mother took a sedative prescribed abroad for nausea. The same drug is now used to treat multiple myeloma. Which drug is it?
questions.explanation: Thalidomide, marketed as a sedative for morning sickness, caused severe limb malformations (phocomelia); its current use in multiple myeloma is on the drug-development lecture (L14) slides. The other teratogens below are outside the slides (standard Step 1 facts). A: Isotretinoin causes craniofacial, CNS and cardiac defects. B: Valproate causes neural tube defects. D: Warfarin causes nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses. E: Lithium causes Ebstein anomaly.
